context: Independent source and preserved-evidence review of the first server-local Guildborne HumanParty6 lifecycle increment on 2026-10-14. Final local Memory candidate 39dfc9420fb57af517370c842c0e09bfd000560539aa0df4dd6db6eea9f803dc. Personal Guild ownership and the saved five-NPC party remain separate; shared combat and reward settlement are not implemented by this increment.
observation: Source review identified an initial adapter branch that treated a connected user's Saving or Degraded profile as a disconnect, which would clear invitations/readiness, transfer leadership and eventually expire membership. The corrected adapter separates connection/session identity from command eligibility. Independent final focused tests passed nine checks, including Saving and Degraded each held longer than the 30-second disconnect grace without member or leader loss, offline grace-member kick and old-session removal refusal. Final UI stub checks permit only Leave, Decline, Disband and Kick in paused profile states and disable all mutations while the controller has a pending request. Preserved Studio raw separately records four synthetic native SliceUI layout cases, same-profile-revision invitation redraw, and actual Network-module routing with fake dependencies and zero profile/economic callbacks.
correction: Do not infer physical disconnect from persistence status. Preserve membership and leadership while the same owned profile/session is Saving or Degraded; use an explicit eligibility flag to refuse new invite, accept, ready and leader-transfer operations. Apply removal/grace only to actual disconnection, closing, ownership/session replacement or terminal loss according to the contract. Retain recipient and session fences, clear replay cache on replacement session, and allow recovery actions to remove disconnected reserved members. Mirror recovery availability in the real paused-state UI, not only the component's Active branch. Test save delays longer than the disconnect grace and drive unsolicited social updates through their own transient revision.
limit: The initially flawed branch was diagnosed by source review, not an independently recorded execution of an unfixed build. The nine core/adapter checks and two UI stub checks are local synthetic results. Studio Network evidence calls actual Network.Intent with fake dependencies and one real local Player transport target; it is not an actual incoming client request roundtrip or multiplayer session. Native SliceUI evidence uses synthetic social state, not a normal six-human route. The 764-test full baseline preceded the final UI recovery refinement; final affected UI analysis, compilation and stub checks were separate. No cloud persistence, server-transfer survival, shared enemy/reward allocation, platform blocking integration, physical hardware, visual approval or human UAT is established. Archived source/test files are exact reference snapshots; their relative requires are not a standalone executable test package. Recording this lesson performs no skill proposal, evaluator, promotion, model call, publishing, spending or permission change.
